key_insight: By combining notched and notch-free microbeam tests with phase-field fracture modeling, the study extracts both the toughness (Gc) and ultimate strength (σc) of amorphous silica from the same framework.
engineering_relevance: The approach provides a practical way to characterize brittle glass in both fracture-driven and strength-controlled regimes, which is valuable for micro- and nano-scale structural design.
method: Fabricate single-notched and bone-shaped amorphous silica microbeams by FIB milling.
Test both geometries in bending in air to probe fracture and strength limits.
Couple experiments with FEA + phase-field fracture simulation to identify Gc, KIC, lc, and σc.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports identified values of Gc = 5.1 J/m², KIC = 0.61 MPa·m^{1/2}, lc = 9.1 nm, and σc = 6.8 GPa, with parametric studies on notch geometry and measurement error.
watch_item: Results depend on FIB-fabricated microbeam geometry and dimensional metrology, so notch shape and measurement error can materially affect the inferred toughness.
paper_title: A Combined Microbeam and Phase-Field Approach to Identify the Toughness and Ultimate Strength of Amorphous Silica
